name: CelesTrak Request Builder Nodes
description: Request-builder flow nodes for CelesTrak ingest (loop C.8a): a module cron TIMER tick enters on 'tick'; each method emits the hostcap/http-request request JSON plus the parser 'job' JSON (source attribution + archive naming). publish_request additionally turns a completed storage-ingest result plus the parser's ingest meta into the dataset-publication POST for the node's loopback admin endpoint (§19), emitting nothing when celestrak_publish_url is unset. cache_warm additionally turns a completed storage-ingest result into the dataset's default-query frame for hostcap/flatsql-query, warming the materialized-cache response artifact on every ingest (graph task sdn-dataset-default-query-materialized-cache). Every request carries a per-lane response byte budget (maxBytes; hostcap/http-request forwards it as max_bytes and the Go host errors past it, never truncates: gp 67108864, satcat 33554432, spw 4194304, eop 4194304, socrates 8388608). Every job carries the upstream origin (origin_id celestrak.org, origin_name CelesTrak, dataset_id gp-full-catalog / satcat / satcat-csv / sw-all / eop-all / socrates-minrange / socrates-maxprob) and the origin's usage terms (license = the usage-policy sentence quoted verbatim, license_url = https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php, citation) so the parser's ingest meta and the host's connector ledger name the organisation the bytes came from. URLs/timeout/provider/defaults are overridable via node CONFIG through the builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall (keys: celestrak_gp_url, celestrak_satcat_url, celestrak_satcat_csv_url, celestrak_space_weather_url, celestrak_http_timeout_ms, celestrak_provider_id, celestrak_publish_url, celestrak_cache_sql, celestrak_cache_max_rows, celestrak_eop_url, celestrak_socrates_minrange_url, celestrak_socrates_maxprob_url, celestrak_gp_max_bytes, celestrak_satcat_max_bytes, celestrak_spw_max_bytes, celestrak_eop_max_bytes, celestrak_socrates_max_bytes, celestrak_license, celestrak_license_url, celestrak_citation) — never via host code. No capabilities: plugin.getConfig is a builtin.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON job attribution for the parser node: {"source_url","source_name","provider_id","archive_source","archive_name","origin_id","origin_name","dataset_id","license","license_url","citation"}.

methods.description: Builds the GP full-catalog fetch request + parse job from a timer tick. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

methods.description: Materialize-on-ingest for the dataset's default FlatSQL query (graph task sdn-dataset-default-query-materialized-cache, celestrak catalog lane): a completed storage-ingest result in 'result' emits the {'sql','params'} frame that hostcap/flatsql-query:query re-executes against the store the same lane just committed, warming the flatsqlrt response-artifact cache the dataset load serves from. SQL comes from node CONFIG key celestrak_cache_sql (default SELECT data FROM sds_omm ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT ? — a bound parameter, never caller-interpolated); the LIMIT comes from celestrak_cache_max_rows (default 5000, server-side clamp). No capabilities: plugin.getConfig is a builtin. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider).
